**The meaning of the verse**
﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اصْبِرُوا وَصَابِرُوا وَرَابِطُوا وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾
O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law: be patient in obeying your Lord and in whatever harm and trial befalls you; outdo your enemies in patience so that they are not more patient than you; remain steadfast in striving against My enemy and your enemy; and fear Allah in all your circumstances, in the hope that you will win His pleasure in this world and the Hereafter.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. Grandpa Abdul-Rahim used to say, "This land is an amanah, a trust." Why did he call it a trust?
2. When the three trees were cut down, what did Grandpa and the people of the village do? And what did Yamen do?
3. Is patience sitting still and doing nothing? (No. The villagers' patience was staying awake, coming together and working, and planting again, along with fearing Allah.)

**This week's exercise**
Your child plants a seed or a seedling in a pot, writes their name on it, and waters it every day this week, even if it is slow to come up. And tell them about something your family inherited and still takes care of.
